prefs.aboutBodyLine1: I loved Google Keep in a "this is exactly how my brain works" way. Open it, write the thing, done. No friction.
prefs.aboutBodyLine2: I spent years looking for a self-hosted replacement and found nothing. Two-pane markdown editors that make you stare at your own syntax. Note apps so bloated it takes four clicks to make a checklist. Nobody built the thing I actually wanted.
prefs.aboutBodyLine4: Freeman Notes is offline-first, runs on hardware you control. You never see the markdown, just the result. Collections, collaboration, permissions — there when you need them, invisible when you don't.
prefs.aboutBodyLine5: The right man in the wrong app can make all the difference in the world.
